en: Air is a mixture of gases that has mass and takes up space, making an inflated balloon heavier than a completely deflated one.
Melting uses heat to change a solid like butter into a liquid, whereas dissolving mixes a solid like sugar evenly throughout water.
Liquid water evaporates into a gas at any temperature, meaning puddles dry up on cool days without ever reaching 100 degrees Celsius.
Not all metals are magnetic, because common metals like aluminum cans, copper wires, and gold jewelry are not attracted to magnets.
The white cloud seen above boiling water is actually tiny liquid water droplets condensing in cooler air, not the invisible water vapor gas.
Rusting is a chemical change because iron reacts with oxygen to form a completely new, irreversible substance called iron oxide.
Air is a gaseous solution made of mixed nitrogen and oxygen gases, proving that solutions do not have to be liquids.
Solid ice and liquid water are the exact same chemical substance, H2O, just existing in different physical states of matter.
Breaking a piece of chalk into many smaller dust particles changes its physical shape but does not change its total mass.
A massive steel ship floats while a tiny pebble sinks because floating depends on an object's overall density, not just its total weight.
The temperature of boiling water stays exactly at 100 degrees Celsius the entire time it boils, rather than getting hotter as it turns to gas.
Gases do not have a fixed volume, because a small amount of compressed oxygen will rapidly expand to fill an entire large room.
